chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about a hunted dove that is worth half a dirham or one dirham. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If you know its owner, return it to him, and if you do not know its owner, and it has level wings, flying with both of them, then it is for you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on keeping a found domesticated bird if the owner is unknown?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the principle of *Dhimmah* (trust) for found property, distinguishing between identifiable and unidentifiable items. The condition of 'equal wings' (*mustawi al-janahayn*) serves as a practical criterion for the bird's viability and value, reflecting the economic realities of 9th-century Kufa. It underscores the Shia emphasis on preserving wealth (*Hifz al-Mal*) while ensuring fairness to the original owner.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about a hunt of the dove equating to half a Dirham, or one Dirham. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When its owner it known, so it would be returned to him, and if its owner is not known, and its wings were levelled, flying with these two, so it is for him’.
en.sarwar: 3. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl who has said the following: “

I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about hunting pigeons worth one-half of a dirham or one dirham. He (the Imam) said, ‘If you know its owner return it to him; but if you do not know its owner and its wings are complete with both of which it can fly then it is yours . 555
